title: Alopecia Areata Totalis
subtitle: An Anatomical Study · 40 Histological Terms in Clinical Context

symptomGroups.title: Total Body Hair Loss
symptomGroups.desc: Scalp, brows, lashes, body, vibrissae all gone

terms.name: ectoderm
terms.definition: The outermost of the three primary germ layers in the early embryo; gives rise to the skin, hair, nails, and the nervous system.
terms.desc: follicles are ectoderm-derived; the autoimmune target
terms.symptom: Hair sheds in clumps over days to weeks — handfuls in the shower, on the pillow — until the scalp, brows, lashes, and body hair are completely gone.

terms.name: epithelial tissue
terms.definition: A type of body tissue made of tightly packed cells that lines surfaces and cavities, including the outer skin, the inside of the digestive tract, and the lining of glands.
terms.desc: follicle is epithelial; what T cells attack
terms.symptom: Hair sheds in clumps over days to weeks — handfuls in the shower, on the pillow — until the scalp, brows, lashes, and body hair are completely gone.

terms.name: matrix
terms.definition: In histology, the actively dividing cells at the base of a hair follicle (the bulb) that produce the hair shaft. More broadly, "matrix" also refers to the non-cellular material surrounding cells in any connective tissue.
terms.symptom: Hair sheds in clumps over days to weeks — handfuls in the shower, on the pillow — until the scalp, brows, lashes, and body hair are completely gone.

terms.name: apoptosis
terms.definition: Programmed cell death — a controlled, energy-requiring process by which a cell self-destructs without harming neighboring cells.
terms.symptom: Hair sheds in clumps over days to weeks — handfuls in the shower, on the pillow — until the scalp, brows, lashes, and body hair are completely gone.

terms.name: mesoderm
terms.definition: The middle of the three primary germ layers in the early embryo; gives rise to muscle, bone, blood, and connective tissue including the dermis of the skin.
terms.symptom: Hair sheds in clumps over days to weeks — handfuls in the shower, on the pillow — until the scalp, brows, lashes, and body hair are completely gone.

terms.name: atrophy
terms.definition: A decrease in the size of a cell, tissue, or organ from a previously normal state — often due to disuse, reduced nutrient supply, or loss of signaling.
terms.symptom: Hair sheds in clumps over days to weeks — handfuls in the shower, on the pillow — until the scalp, brows, lashes, and body hair are completely gone.

terms.name: basal lamina
terms.definition: A thin sheet of extracellular matrix produced by epithelial cells, sitting just beneath them and separating epithelium from underlying connective tissue.
terms.symptom: Hair around the bald spots pulls out painlessly with a light tug; short, broken stubble rings the edges where new patches are still spreading.

terms.name: basement membrane
terms.definition: A specialized layer at the boundary between an epithelium and its connective tissue, made of the basal lamina plus an underlying reticular layer of collagen fibers.
terms.desc: T cells cross BM to reach the bulb
terms.symptom: Hair around the bald spots pulls out painlessly with a light tug; short, broken stubble rings the edges where new patches are still spreading.

terms.name: anchoring junction
terms.definition: A type of cell junction (such as a desmosome or adherens junction) that mechanically links neighboring cells together so tissues can resist pulling forces.
terms.symptom: Hair around the bald spots pulls out painlessly with a light tug; short, broken stubble rings the edges where new patches are still spreading.

terms.name: apical
terms.definition: The surface of an epithelial cell that faces the outside world or a hollow space (lumen), opposite the basal surface that sits on the basement membrane.
terms.symptom: Hair around the bald spots pulls out painlessly with a light tug; short, broken stubble rings the edges where new patches are still spreading.

terms.name: ground substance
terms.definition: The clear, gel-like material in the extracellular matrix of connective tissue that fills the space between cells and fibers; made of water, proteoglycans, and glycoproteins.
terms.symptom: Hair around the bald spots pulls out painlessly with a light tug; short, broken stubble rings the edges where new patches are still spreading.

terms.name: inflammation
terms.definition: The body's protective response to injury or infection, marked by redness, heat, swelling, pain, and sometimes loss of function as immune cells flood the affected area.
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: histamine
terms.definition: A chemical signal released mainly by mast cells that triggers itching, redness, swelling, and increased blood-vessel leakiness during allergic and inflammatory responses.
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: vasodilation
terms.definition: The widening of blood vessels caused by relaxation of the smooth muscle in their walls, increasing blood flow and producing redness and warmth.
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: endothelium
terms.definition: The single layer of flat epithelial cells lining the inside of all blood vessels and the heart, regulating what passes between blood and surrounding tissue.
terms.desc: adhesion molecules let T cells exit vessels
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: fluid connective tissue
terms.definition: Connective tissue with a liquid extracellular matrix — namely blood and lymph — that carries cells and substances throughout the body.
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: areolar tissue
terms.definition: A loose connective tissue with a soft, jelly-like ground substance and loosely arranged collagen and elastic fibers; cushions and supports nearby structures.
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: loose connective tissue
terms.definition: A broad category of connective tissues with widely spaced fibers and abundant ground substance — includes areolar, adipose, and reticular tissue; cushions, insulates, and surrounds organs and vessels.
terms.symptom: The bald spots itch, look pink, feel warm, and are sore to the touch.

terms.name: collagen fiber
terms.definition: A strong, rope-like protein fiber found throughout connective tissue that gives tissues their tensile strength and resists stretching.
terms.symptom: The bald skin stays smooth and unmarked — no bumps, no scars, no pitting — looking just like ordinary skin without hair.

terms.name: elastic fiber
terms.definition: A protein fiber made mostly of elastin that allows tissues to stretch and recoil to their original shape; abundant in skin, lungs, and large arteries.
terms.symptom: The bald skin stays smooth and unmarked — no bumps, no scars, no pitting — looking just like ordinary skin without hair.

terms.name: reticular fiber
terms.definition: A thin, branching collagen fiber that forms a delicate supporting network in soft organs like the liver, spleen, and lymph nodes.
terms.symptom: The bald skin stays smooth and unmarked — no bumps, no scars, no pitting — looking just like ordinary skin without hair.

terms.name: connective tissue
terms.definition: A diverse category of body tissue characterized by widely spaced cells embedded in an extracellular matrix; binds, supports, protects, and stores energy.
terms.symptom: The bald skin stays smooth and unmarked — no bumps, no scars, no pitting — looking just like ordinary skin without hair.

terms.name: dense connective tissue (irregular/regular)
terms.definition: Connective tissue packed with closely arranged collagen fibers; "regular" types (like tendons) have parallel fibers for one-direction strength, while "irregular" types (like the dermis) have woven fibers for multi-direction strength.
terms.symptom: The bald skin stays smooth and unmarked — no bumps, no scars, no pitting — looking just like ordinary skin without hair.

terms.name: gap junction
terms.definition: A type of cell junction containing protein channels that directly connect the cytoplasm of two neighboring cells, allowing ions and small molecules to pass between them for rapid signaling.
terms.symptom: When hair grows back, it comes in as fine, fuzzy peach-colored or white strands instead of normal pigmented hair — and it often falls out again.

terms.name: tight junction
terms.definition: A type of cell junction that seals adjacent epithelial cells together to prevent fluids and molecules from leaking between them, creating a barrier.
terms.symptom: When hair grows back, it comes in as fine, fuzzy peach-colored or white strands instead of normal pigmented hair — and it often falls out again.

terms.name: fibroblast
terms.definition: The most common cell in connective tissue; secretes the proteins (collagen, elastin) and ground substance that make up the extracellular matrix.
terms.symptom: When hair grows back, it comes in as fine, fuzzy peach-colored or white strands instead of normal pigmented hair — and it often falls out again.

terms.name: adipocytes
terms.definition: Specialized connective tissue cells that store energy as fat in a single large lipid droplet, also providing insulation and cushioning.
terms.desc: stem cell signaling lost; regrowth delayed
terms.symptom: When hair grows back, it comes in as fine, fuzzy peach-colored or white strands instead of normal pigmented hair — and it often falls out again.

terms.name: adipose tissue
terms.definition: Connective tissue dominated by adipocytes (fat cells); stores energy, insulates the body, cushions organs, and produces hormones.
terms.symptom: When hair grows back, it comes in as fine, fuzzy peach-colored or white strands instead of normal pigmented hair — and it often falls out again.

terms.name: cutaneous membrane
terms.definition: Another name for the skin — the largest organ of the body, composed of an epidermis (epithelium) sitting on a dermis (connective tissue).
terms.symptom: Without hair, the scalp sunburns easily, sweat drips into the eyes without brows to catch it, dust irritates the eyes without lashes, the ears feel cold, and goosebumps no longer appear.

terms.name: stratified squamous epithelium
terms.definition: Epithelial tissue made of multiple layers of flat cells; found wherever surfaces face mechanical wear, such as the skin, mouth, and esophagus.
terms.symptom: Without hair, the scalp sunburns easily, sweat drips into the eyes without brows to catch it, dust irritates the eyes without lashes, the ears feel cold, and goosebumps no longer appear.

terms.name: neuron
terms.definition: An excitable cell of the nervous system that transmits information by generating and propagating electrical signals along its membrane.
terms.symptom: Without hair, the scalp sunburns easily, sweat drips into the eyes without brows to catch it, dust irritates the eyes without lashes, the ears feel cold, and goosebumps no longer appear.

terms.name: nervous tissue
terms.definition: Body tissue made of neurons and supporting glial cells; specialized to receive, process, and transmit electrical signals throughout the body.
terms.symptom: Without hair, the scalp sunburns easily, sweat drips into the eyes without brows to catch it, dust irritates the eyes without lashes, the ears feel cold, and goosebumps no longer appear.

terms.name: smooth muscle
terms.definition: Involuntary, non-striated muscle tissue found in the walls of hollow organs and blood vessels, producing slow, sustained contractions.
terms.symptom: Without hair, the scalp sunburns easily, sweat drips into the eyes without brows to catch it, dust irritates the eyes without lashes, the ears feel cold, and goosebumps no longer appear.

terms.name: merocrine secretion
terms.definition: A mode of glandular secretion in which the cell releases its product (usually by exocytosis) without losing any cytoplasm — the most common method, used by sweat glands and salivary glands.
terms.desc: visible sweating; no hair to trap moisture
terms.symptom: Skin and scalp feel drier than before, sweat shows more visibly without hair to absorb it, and body odor is noticeably reduced.

terms.name: holocrine secretion
terms.definition: A mode of glandular secretion in which the entire cell ruptures and dies to release its contents — used by sebaceous (oil) glands.
terms.symptom: Skin and scalp feel drier than before, sweat shows more visibly without hair to absorb it, and body odor is noticeably reduced.

terms.name: apocrine secretion
terms.definition: A mode of glandular secretion in which the apical (top) portion of the cell pinches off and is released along with the product — used by certain sweat glands and mammary glands.
terms.symptom: Skin and scalp feel drier than before, sweat shows more visibly without hair to absorb it, and body odor is noticeably reduced.

terms.name: exocrine gland
terms.definition: A gland that releases its secretion through a duct onto an epithelial surface — examples include sweat, salivary, and sebaceous glands.
terms.symptom: Skin and scalp feel drier than before, sweat shows more visibly without hair to absorb it, and body odor is noticeably reduced.

terms.name: reticular tissue
terms.definition: A loose connective tissue made up of a delicate network of reticular fibers, forming the supportive framework (stroma) of lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow.
terms.desc: lymph node stroma primes autoreactive T cells
terms.symptom: During flares, swollen, tender lumps can be felt at the back of the neck, in the armpits, or in the groin.

terms.name: endocrine gland
terms.definition: A ductless gland that releases its hormones directly into the bloodstream rather than onto a surface — examples include the thyroid, adrenals, and pituitary.
terms.symptom: May also experience fatigue, cold intolerance, weight changes, or a racing heart from a co-existing thyroid problem.

histologyPlates.title: Hair Follicle & Pilosebaceous Unit
histologyPlates.imageAlt: Cross-section of skin showing hair follicle, sebaceous gland, and arrector pili muscle
histologyPlates.caption: The autoimmune target itself. The bulb (matrix), papilla, inner and outer root sheaths, and surrounding glands form the pilosebaceous unit. CD8⁺ T cells breach the basal lamina to attack matrix cells. Note the arrector pili (smooth muscle) and sebaceous gland (holocrine) attached to the follicle.
histologyPlates.attribution: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy (1918), Plate 944. Public domain.

histologyPlates.title: Vertical Section of Skin (Magnified)
histologyPlates.imageAlt: Vertical section of skin showing epidermis, dermis, and underlying connective tissue
histologyPlates.caption: The cutaneous membrane in vertical section. Stratified squamous epithelium of the epidermis sits on the basement membrane; the dermis below contains areolar and dense connective tissue, with collagen, elastic, and reticular fibers in ground substance. Endothelium-lined vessels deliver immune cells.
histologyPlates.attribution: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy (1918). Public domain.

histologyPlates.title: Lymph Node — Reticular Architecture
histologyPlates.imageAlt: Diagram of a lymph node showing cortex, medulla, and reticular structure
histologyPlates.caption: Where autoreactive T cells are primed before trafficking to the follicle. The node's reticular tissue (a network of reticular fibers) supports germinal centers in the cortex; tender posterior cervical, occipital, axillary, and inguinal nodes during AT flares reflect activity here.
histologyPlates.attribution: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy (1918). Public domain.

histologyPlates.title: Thyroid Gland — Anterior View
histologyPlates.imageAlt: Anterior view of the thyroid gland showing lobes and isthmus
histologyPlates.caption: Strong autoimmune comorbidity with AT — Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Graves' disease co-occur in 8–28% of cases. Clinical workup for AT routinely screens TSH. The thyroid is an endocrine gland (ductless, secreting directly into blood), distinguishing it from the exocrine glands of the pilosebaceous unit.
histologyPlates.attribution: Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy (1918). Public domain.
